tec-vulnscan.summary: A tool that regularly checks every server, laptop, network device and web app for known weaknesses and missing patches.
tec-vulnscan.protects: Servers, endpoints, network devices, cloud workloads and internet-facing apps, against attackers exploiting known vulnerabilities (CVEs) and misconfigurations.
tec-vulnscan.placement: Central console (cloud or on-premises) with scanners in each network zone (DMZ, data centre, each site) plus light agents on laptops and servers; owned by the security testing or vulnerability management lead.
tec-vulnscan.how: Scanners probe assets on a schedule and agents report installed software. Findings are matched to CVE databases and ranked by severity and exploit likelihood (CVSS, EPSS, CISA KEV). Tickets go to asset owners with a fix deadline, and a rescan proves the fix.
pareto: A complete asset inventory, so nothing goes unscanned
Authenticated (credentialed) scans or agents, not just network scans
Weekly scans of everything internet-facing
Risk-based ranking (known-exploited first) with fix SLAs per severity
Rescan to verify closure, and a monthly ageing report to management

vendors.name: Tenable (Nessus, Tenable Vulnerability Management, Tenable One)
vendors.fit: Widely used scanner with broad plugin coverage; Nessus Professional suits small teams, Tenable VM suits a full estate.
vendors.india: Sold through Indian distributors and partners; India sales office.

vendors.name: Qualys VMDR
vendors.fit: Cloud platform with agents, scanning and patch add-on in one console; strong for large, spread-out estates.
vendors.india: Large engineering centre in Pune; Indian partners; check the hosting region for scan data.

vendors.name: Rapid7 InsightVM (now packaged in Exposure Command)
vendors.fit: Good risk scoring and remediation tracking; per-asset pricing published historically.

vendors.name: SecPod Saner CVEM
vendors.fit: Bengaluru-based vendor combining scanning and patching in one agent; choose when an Indian vendor and built-in remediation matter.

vendors.name: Greenbone OpenVAS (Community Edition)
vendors.fit: Free network vulnerability scanner; fits labs, small estates or a second-opinion scanner. Needs in-house skill; paid Greenbone Enterprise appliances exist.
vendors.india: No local vendor support for the free edition; community only.

Add-ons: web app scanning, patching, cloud posture, external attack surface
Agent versus scanner model

Credentialed scanning for Windows, Linux, network devices and major databases

tec-vulnscan.architecture: Console in the cloud or the data centre; one scanner appliance or VM per network zone (DMZ, server zone, each of 5 sites) reaching assets over allowed ports; agents on laptops and servers report outbound. It reads the asset inventory (CMDB, AD, cloud APIs) and feeds tickets to the ITSM tool, findings to the SIEM and risk register, and fix status to management dashboards.

Reports go out but nobody owns the fix or the deadline

tec-logging.summary: Collecting the logs from every important system into one protected place, with correct clocks, and keeping them long enough to investigate and to meet the law.
tec-logging.protects: The evidence trail: who did what, when, on firewalls, identity, endpoints, servers, cloud and key apps. Without it, attacks go unseen and cannot be investigated or reported.
tec-logging.placement: Log collectors in each data centre and site; a central log store (on-premises or an India cloud region) in the management or security zone; owned by the SOC manager, with IT owning the sources.
tec-logging.how: Each system sends logs (syslog, agents, cloud APIs) to collectors, which buffer, parse and forward them to a central store. Every system takes its time from NTP servers of NIC or NPL, or servers traceable to them, so timelines line up. Logs are kept tamper-evident for at least 180 days in India, with hot search for recent data and cheaper archive for the rest.
pareto: Clock sync on every system to NIC/NPL-traceable NTP, monitored for drift
The top sources first: firewalls, VPN, AD/identity, EDR, email, DNS, cloud audit logs, critical apps
180-day rolling retention in India, protected from deletion (WORM or immutable storage)
Alert when a key source stops sending logs
A written log source list with owner, volume and retention

vendors.fit: Mature collection and search at scale; licence by daily ingest or workload, so storing everything can be costly.

vendors.fit: Free core for collection, search and retention with tiered storage; paid licences add security features and support.

vendors.india: Community and Indian integrators; self-hosted in India.

vendors.india: Data stays in India; check MeitY empanelment.

tec-logging.architecture: Sources (firewalls, VPN, AD, EDR, servers, cloud, apps) send to collectors at each site and data centre; collectors buffer and forward over TLS to the central log store in India (hot tier for recent search, archive tier for 180 days and more). The store feeds the SIEM, the SOC and investigators. Internal NTP servers in each data centre take time from NIC/NPL and serve all devices.
kpis: Percentage of critical sources sending logs in the last 24 hours (target 100%)
Maximum clock drift across sources
Days of retention actually available, tested by a restore
Hours from a source going silent to an alert
pitfalls: Keeping logs in a foreign cloud region and assuming it meets CERT-In
No clock sync, so events from different systems cannot be lined up
Collecting everything into an expensive SIEM tier instead of archiving bulk logs
Never testing that old logs can actually be restored and searched

tec-siem.summary: A security monitoring platform that reads logs from across the organisation and raises alerts when it sees signs of an attack.
tec-siem.protects: The whole estate, by detecting intrusions, account misuse, malware spread and data theft that individual tools miss.
tec-siem.placement: Central platform (SaaS in an India region, or on-premises in the data centre security zone) fed by log collectors; operated by the SOC, owned by the SOC manager.
tec-siem.how: Logs are parsed and stored, then detection rules and analytics look for patterns mapped to MITRE ATT&CK. Alerts go to analysts with context, and the SIEM keeps the search history for investigations. Rules are tuned every month to cut noise and fill gaps.
pareto: The right 10-15 log sources onboarded well before adding more
20-30 high-value detections mapped to ATT&CK (identity abuse, ransomware precursors, privilege use, data exfiltration)
Monthly tuning that removes noisy rules and adds missing ones
Alert triage with clear severity and an owner
Detection coverage reviewed after every incident and BAS run

tec-soc.summary: A team, in-house, outsourced or mixed, that watches security alerts around the clock and responds to attacks.
tec-soc.protects: The whole organisation, by turning alerts into fast containment of intrusions, ransomware and account takeover at any hour.
tec-soc.placement: A process and people function run by the SOC manager under the CISO; analysts in a secure room or remote, or at a managed provider's SOC in India, working on the SIEM, EDR and SOAR consoles.
tec-soc.how: Analysts in shifts triage alerts (L1), investigate and contain (L2), and hunt and engineer detections (L3). Runbooks say who does what, and severe incidents go to the incident response team and leadership. Regulated entities report to CERT-In within 6 hours and to their regulator as required.
pareto: True 24x7 coverage with a named escalation path to someone who can isolate a host or disable an account
Runbooks for the top 10 incident types (phishing, ransomware, account takeover, malware, data leak)
EDR on all endpoints plus the SIEM, so the SOC can see and act
Clear SLAs: time to triage, time to escalate, time to contain
Monthly service review with metrics and detection improvements

Digital risk monitoring watches for leaked data, look-alike domains and brand abuse.

tec-soar.summary: Software that runs response steps automatically or at one click, so routine alerts are handled in seconds and analysts focus on real attacks.
tec-soar.protects: The SOC's speed and consistency: faster containment of phishing, malware and compromised accounts, and fewer human errors under pressure.
tec-soar.placement: Automation platform in the SOC tool set (SaaS or on-premises), connected by API to SIEM, EDR, email, identity, firewall and ticketing; owned by the SOC manager, built by a SOC engineer.
tec-soar.how: A playbook starts when an alert arrives: it enriches it (reputation, user, asset), decides or asks an analyst, then acts (quarantine email, isolate host, disable account, block indicator) and records every step in a case. Low-risk actions run automatically; high-impact ones need approval.
pareto: Phishing triage: extract, check and purge reported emails
Alert enrichment for every alert (user, asset, reputation)
One-click host isolation and account disablement with approval
Indicator blocking across firewall, proxy and EDR
Automatic case creation and evidence capture for reporting

tec-ueba.summary: Analytics that learn how each user and device normally behaves and raise an alert when behaviour changes in a risky way; XDR joins endpoint, identity, email and network signals into one detection and response view.
tec-ueba.protects: Accounts and data, against stolen credentials, insider misuse, lateral movement and slow data theft that rule-based alerts miss.
tec-ueba.placement: An analytics layer in the SIEM or XDR platform (cloud service), fed by identity, endpoint, VPN, email and app logs; owned by the SOC manager.
tec-ueba.how: The tool builds a baseline per user, peer group and device (logon times, places, volumes, systems used). It scores deviations, such as an impossible journey or mass file access, and combines them into a risk score. High scores create alerts or trigger extra checks such as forced MFA.

Watch lists for privileged users and leavers

Joined-up XDR view so one incident is not ten alerts

tec-bas.summary: A tool that safely imitates real attack techniques inside the network, again and again, to prove whether the security controls actually stop or detect them.
tec-bas.protects: Confidence in every other control: finds gaps in EDR, email security, firewalls, SIEM rules and segmentation before an attacker does.
tec-bas.placement: Management console (SaaS or on-premises) with simulation agents on a sample of endpoints and servers in each zone; owned by the security testing lead, with results shared with the SOC (purple teaming).
tec-bas.how: Agents run harmless versions of attacker techniques mapped to MITRE ATT&CK, such as credential dumping, lateral movement or data exfiltration. The tool checks whether each was blocked, detected (alert in SIEM/EDR) or missed. Gaps become tickets and new detections, and the test is rerun to prove the fix.
pareto: Agents in every key zone (user VLAN, server zone, DMZ, cloud)
Ransomware and credential-theft scenarios first
Check detection in the SIEM, not only blocking
Monthly or weekly scheduled runs with trend reports
Every gap goes into the vulnerability or detection backlog with an owner

tec-deception.summary: Fake systems, files and credentials placed among real ones, so that any attacker who touches them sets off a reliable alarm.
tec-deception.protects: The internal network and key data, by catching intruders and insiders early, during reconnaissance and lateral movement, with almost no false alarms.
tec-deception.placement: Decoy devices (hardware or VMs) in the DMZ, server zone, user VLANs and cloud; decoy tokens (fake credentials, documents, cloud keys) on endpoints and file shares; alerts go to the SOC; owned by the SOC manager.
tec-deception.how: Decoys pretend to be servers, databases, switches or file shares; nothing legitimate should ever touch them. Tokens such as a fake admin password or document call home when used. Any interaction sends a high-confidence alert to the SIEM and SOC.
pareto: A few decoys in each key segment (server zone, user VLAN, DMZ)
Fake credentials and files on endpoints and shares (honeytokens)
Decoys that look like the crown jewels (core banking, payments, backups)
Every alert treated as a real incident with a runbook
Low effort: managed decoys that update themselves
